A veces el Sol lanza explosiones de ener: Sometimes the Sun throws out bursts of energy (solar flares) and huge clouds of particles (coronal mass ejections). All of this is called space weather.

El Sol lanza partículas chiquitísimas y: The Sun throws out super tiny, super fast particles, like an invisible rain. Mars has almost no air to stop them, so they reach the ground. The base's radiation goes up! It's dangerous outside: anyone who goes out loses health faster.

El monte Olimpo (Olympus Mons) es el vol: Olympus Mons is the biggest volcano in the solar system. It's about 22 kilometers high: more than twice as tall as Mount Everest!

En el centro del cráter hay una montaña: In the middle of the crater there's a mountain called Mount Sharp. It has rocks with clays and sulfates (a kind of salt). Those minerals need water to form. That's why scientists thought Gale had water a long time ago!
En la cima tiene un cráter enorme, es de: At the top it has a huge crater, meaning it's a volcano!: it erupted many times and the lava kept making it bigger. It hasn't erupted for millions of years.
Encontrar señales de que hubo agua en Ma: Finding signs that there was water on Mars is exciting because it means the planet could have had life a long time ago.

Entre junio y agosto de 1976 llegaron a: Between June and August 1976, two sister probes reached Mars: Viking 1 and Viking 2. They wanted to learn more about the planet and find out whether there was ever life.
Esas partículas pueden dañar los aparato: Those particles can damage spacecraft equipment and put astronauts at risk. That's why NASA logs every event in a database called DONKI and warns missions when a solar storm is coming.
